desc: It's a thing you climb to reach something high, with steps between two long sides.
It's the person who owns the flat you rent and who you pay every month.
It's a small instrument you use to check how hot or cold something is, or whether you have a fever.
It's the journey you make every day between your home and your workplace.
It's an office tool that joins sheets of paper together with a small piece of metal.
It's the list of ingredients and instructions that tells you how to cook a dish.
It's something you open and hold over your head to keep the rain off.
It's a small thing you buy on holiday to remind you of the place.
It's someone who works at the same company as you.
It's the date or time by which you have to finish a piece of work.
It's the shop where you go to get medicine, sometimes with a prescription from the doctor.
It's when there are so many cars on the road that they can hardly move.
It's a tall piece of furniture in the bedroom where you hang your clothes.
It's that warm, slightly sad feeling you get when you think about happy times in the past.
It's money that a university or organisation gives a student to pay for their studies, often because they did very well.
It's a machine where you put in money or tap a card and it gives you a drink or a snack.
It means to keep putting off something you should do, doing other things instead.
It's a residential area on the edge of a city, quieter than the centre.
It's the cable and plug you use to put power back into your phone's battery.
It's someone who works for a charity or event without being paid.
